Write a self-contained Rust 2024 program (standard library only) that computes the first 200 prime numbers two independent ways and cross-checks them.

Requirements:
1. Method A (trial division): find primes in order by testing each candidate n>=2 for divisibility by all previously found primes up to sqrt(n); collect until 200 primes.
2. Method B (sieve): Sieve of Eratosthenes over a range large enough to contain at least 200 primes (e.g., upper bound 2000, verified by counting); collect the first 200 primes from it.
3. Assert the two lists are identical element-by-element (assert_eq! on the Vec<u64>s). If they disagree, panic.
4. Compute count (=200), sum of the 200 primes, and the largest (200th) prime. Known reference values you may assert against: count==200, largest==1223, sum==111587. Assert these too.
5. Write /work/artifacts/result.json (create the directory if needed) containing a JSON object with keys: "count" (200), "sum" (111587), "largest" (1223), "check" ("agree" when both methods match), and optionally "first_primes" (first few) and "last_primes" (last few).
6. Print a short summary to stdout. Program must run offline in the sandbox within limits; no external crates.
